study_identification_part.si4_title: Cell type-specific manifestations of cortical thickness heterogeneity in schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To determine whether individual cortical thickness (CTh) heterogeneity in schizophrenia aligns with interregional variation in neural cell-type gene expression and to validate cell-based subtypes using person-specific genetic risk (PRS).

rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: This study comprised a total of 1849 participants drawn from three independent datasets: (1) the Human Connectome Project-Young Adult Sample; (2) the Human Connectome Project for Early Psychosis (HCP-psychosis); and (3) the Australian Schizophrenia Research Bank (ASRB).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Correlated each individual’s regional CTh deviation profile with cell-type gene expression maps across 34 regions, clustered subjects into three cell-based subtypes (gap statistic, t-SNE). Validated subtypes by correlating subtype-matched polygenic risk scores (PRS) with deviation severity (e.g., neuronal/endothelial subtype r=-0.40, p=0.010; glia/OPC subtype r=-0.30, p=0.028).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: CTh heterogeneity in schizophrenia aligns with cell-type gene expression patterns, enabling biologically informed subtyping that is supported by subtype-specific genetic risk associations.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Across 1,849 participants (discovery: 140 SZ, 1,127 HC; validation: 335 SZ, 185 HC), normative modeling (quantile regression by age/sex) defined ROI-wise CTh percentiles and z-score deviations. Correlating individual deviation profiles with seven cell-type expression maps revealed meaningful alignment for neuronal/endothelial and glia/OPC cell types. Three cell-based subtypes emerged, with a predominantly neuronal/endothelial subtype (~22% of patients) showing covariance between deviation severity and neuron/endothelial PRS (r=-0.40, p=0.010), and a predominantly glia/OPC subtype (~43%) showing covariance with glia/OPC PRS (r=-0.30, p=0.028). Results replicated in the independent ASRB cohort, supporting multi-scale links between genome, transcriptome, and MRI-derived phenotypes.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative modeling reduces the need for tightly age/sex-matched groups because percentiles are defined on healthy controls as a function of age and sex (applicability note).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Gene expression maps are derived from neurotypical postmortem donors and aligned to the left hemisphere only; normative model performance metrics (e.g., EV, MSLL) are not reported; site/scanner effects are addressed via retrospective ComBat harmonization; mechanistic interpretations remain indirect.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Processing used FreeSurfer (HCP v5.3; ASRB v6.0) with Desikan–Killiany ROIs; harmonization via ComBat verified by ANCOVA. Supplementary figures also depict surface area and gyrification deviations, though the main analyses focus on cortical thickness. Gene expression alignment uses AHBA data mapped to 34 LH regions.
